text:
Cale Makar had the Avalanche holding their breath this week, and then told the Denver Post he "feels really good" and played. He skipped Thursday's morning skate in Ottawa along with Nathan MacKinnon, which the Post's Corey Masisak read as probably nothing.

When he plays, he's doing Makar things: 23 points in 18 games, with Colorado taking 58% of the expected goals at five on five when he's on, almost nine points better than without him. His shooting is normal; the assists are piling up a little faster than the chances (14 points in his last ten against 11 expected), so his rate sits above our range.

Evolving-Hockey had him 12th among defensemen in wins above replacement last season, with the note that his teammates rank among the league's best. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still has him in the 98th percentile for chances from the slot for a defenseman. Our range: 74 to 101 points.
